column1: # When GNU compresses a wide instruction — DERIVED, do not edit.
# `add s0, s0, s1` is two bytes and `add s0, s1, a0` is four. Nothing
# in spec/encodings-riscv64.tsv says why: the fusion conditions live in
# the C extension's semantics, not in any field layout. So they are
# observed, the same way B-037 observed the field positions.
# `-` means the assembler left it wide.
# `relation` is the operand coincidence the probe carries.
# `add s0, s0, s1` and `add s0, zero, s1` both reduce to two
# registers and become c.add and c.mv — DIFFERENT instructions — so
# the reduction does not say which encoding is meant and the relation
# does. That is the fact no field layout can hold.
